name: Serrapeptase (serratiopeptidase)
short: Case reports: drug-induced pneumonitis, one with acute respiratory failure and coughing blood in an 84-year-old man. A systematic review found safety and long-term safety data lacking.
text: A systematic review of 24 clinical studies found the evidence for serratiopeptidase to be of poor methodology, stated that data on its safety and tolerability were lacking in these studies and that data on long-term safety are lacking. A Cochrane review of treatments for breast engorgement reported that no women experienced adverse events in the groups receiving serrapeptase (a comparison of 59 women), protease or placebo (low-certainty evidence). Case reports describe drug-induced lung injury: a 69-year-old man developed interstitial pneumonia after 16 days of serrapeptase for a common cold, which improved once it was stopped, and an 84-year-old man with fever, cough and coughing up blood had acute eosinophilic pneumonia with acute respiratory failure after 3 months of serrapeptase, recovered rapidly after corticosteroids, and later had a positive lymphocyte stimulation test to the drug. A review describes serratiopeptidase as having anti-coagulant activity and breaking down fibrin; none of the cited abstracts report bleeding attributed to an anti-clotting effect. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
